newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank dips after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank dips after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in Royal Bank of Scotland Plc dropped in early trading on Wednesday as the group posted first-half profits no better than analysts had expected, dealers and analyts said.

The stock was down 9-1/2p at 576 by 0819 GMT in active trade of 2.1 million shares. Pre-tax profit rose 14 percent to 369 million stg in the six months to March 31, compared with analyst expectations mostly in a range between 345 million stg and 383 million.

Analysts and dealers said the bank's UK results showing a 24 percent rise in UK banking profits were strong yet the result overall was no better than expected, a slight disappointment after recent positive surprises in UK bank results.
Bank of Scotland Plc, up 1/2p at 393, for instance last month posted a better-than-expected 22 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 664.1 million stg.

"Maybe expectations for the Royal Bank's results crept up following the Bank of Scotland results," said Ian Poulter, analyst at Williams de Broe. "The results are OK and the UK within that is looking good... but it is a bit like damning with faint praise."

Dealers pointed out that Royal Bank shares had risen sharply since the middle of last month, in line with general gains in the bank sector. At yesterday's close the stock was up 12 percent in the past four weeks.
"They have had a good run and we are just seeing some profit-taking," said one market-maker.

Chairman Lord Younger said the first-half results and the "...excellent progress made in developing both existing and new businesses provide a firm foundation from which the group can move forward with confidence."
